method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading and reverse paraphrase of the definition, normalization argument, diagram, proposition and exercises, with exact formula, macro, transition, identifier and reference parity. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Four-clause disciplined-machine normal form, suggested conversion, disciplined addition example, behavior-preserving proposition and two construction exercises.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A disciplined machine has exactly one designated halting state h; if it halts it scans square 1; it never erases the end marker on square 0; and it never tries to move left from square 0. The source contrasts these restrictions with its general machine convention, which permits overwriting the marker and clamps a left move at zero.
samples.checks: All four conjunctive clauses, both square indices, conditional halting and the unrestricted-model comparison are retained in their original order.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: One adds h and redirects every originally undefined state-symbol transition to (h,sigma,N). A general construction is asserted to preserve each input's halting status and output, with a suggested final head move left to the boundary, right one square and halt. Because the old marker could be erased or copied, that marker search is only an illustrative shortcut, not a complete arbitrary-machine proof.
samples.checks: The delta tuple, old-undefined precondition, input/output preservation and three-step suggested move are unchanged. OLTUR-006 adds a limited caveat without inventing an algorithm.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The addition example extends the earlier adder with a leftward return and a transition to h at the end marker. The proposition says every machine M has a disciplined M-prime with the same output whenever M halts and with nonhalting preserved, hence any Turing-computable natural-number function is disciplined-computable.
samples.checks: All diagram transitions, h endpoint, prior-adder reference, output O, both halting directions and function type are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exercises ask for a disciplined successor machine and a disciplined copier taking n strokes to two n-stroke blocks separated by a blank.
samples.checks: Both fixed problem labels and exact input/output expressions are preserved.

source_observations: OLTUR-006 records that the frozen example's search for an end marker is not a complete conversion for a machine allowed to erase the original marker or write copies elsewhere; it does not refute the proposition's existence claim.
T342 uses the source-defined four-clause meaning of शिस्तबद्ध; the complete compound is not presented as an official dictionary headword.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The source omits the complete constructive proof of the normal-form proposition; the Marathi text does not claim to supply one.
